name: AECi — Retention prune deleted an unexpected number of rows
message:
The daily 03:00 UTC §7.4 retention prune (AECI-584) deleted more rows in one day than a steady-state run should. Expected volumes once the windows start biting: ~1,000/day for `page_views` (400-day window, first deletes ~2027-07) and ~120/day for `job_runs` (90-day window, first deletes ~2026-11). A spike means one of: a shortened `PAGE_VIEWS_RETENTION_DAYS` / `JOB_RUNS_RETENTION_DAYS` env override took effect, the cron stopped firing for a stretch and is now catching up, or a traffic surge inflated the day being cut.

This is the alert §7.4 asks for by name: a runaway prune must be visible in Datadog BEFORE it is visible as missing data. Deletion is irreversible past D1 Time Travel's ~30 days, so treat a genuine surprise as an incident: check `PAGE_VIEWS_RETENTION_DAYS` / `JOB_RUNS_RETENTION_DAYS` on the production Worker first (they should be UNSET), then the single `retention.pruned` audit row for the run — `select metadata from audit_log where action = 'retention.pruned' order by created_at desc limit 5` — which records the cutoff and per-table counts. A run that hit its own per-table budget also emits `aeci.retention.prune.truncated`.

Split `by {table}` so a `job_runs` catch-up does not read as a `page_views` incident. Threshold is a launch tunable — raise it once real steady-state volume is observed.

Note: this monitor deliberately does NOT use notify_no_data — `aeci.retention.rows_deleted` IS emitted every run including zeros, so liveness is covered by 'AECi — Retention prune not running' instead.

Runbook: https://github.com/the-wbs-project/aec-integrations/blob/main/docs/RUNBOOKS.md#retention-prune-skipped-failed-or-not-running
